nobox.final_span:
our guest coming in and going to the next table, and the next table asks us if we're cooking their food, and we say 'yes' and we cook this and this and this over and over again. We don't have plenty of space, but we just cooked a great dinner for them.
Have you ever tried a restaurant dish that you felt you could improve upon and make better?
Nguyen: Yeah, in fact, last week I visited another Vietnamese restaurant. It is close to here, yet I wish I had never gone there again. Soft shell crab...I am not sure how to do it.
• Quang Nguyen, 42, reports he never got to really enjoy eating food during the nearly three months he was unconscious following a motorcycle accident on St. Charles Road in May, but he's happy to be back at 390 Greg Boulevard. He now operates Loan Office Vietnamese Restaurant, which serves fresh versions of Vietnamese food, including grilled banh mi sandwiches and fried rice.
• Sankar Sinnakarrappa, 50, and his wife Sunia are celebrating the grand opening of Mi Cocinas, an upscale Mexican restaurant with red leather booths, waiters in white jackets and intimate lighting. The menu even features quesadillas, which aren't particularly common in a Mexican restaurant.
• What would normally be a quiet break between school years turned out to be an enormous challenge for Niles School District 219's Nerf Nights program.
Before they knew it, family members were sworn to secrecy: Over 13,000 Nerf shooting bullets were handmade by kindergartners and crafted by second-graders across 52 classrooms in the district’s numerous venues.
Each year, Nerf Night includes 75 classrooms with 1,000 students participating. It's a science, technology, engineering, math and the arts program for families, where 2:30 to 5:30 p.m. on a designated day is the time to build, throw and aim your Uncle Rico Film Character Nerf Board — named for the character
